hypotheses.construction_plan: Substitute the mapped function symbols and argument variable into the template F(z)*K(z)*F(z). For the first member set F=V, K=G0, z=p; for the second set F=W, K=H0, z=q. The resulting expressions match exactly.
required_assumptions: V, G0, W, H0 are scalar-valued functions on their respective domains
The formal product of scalar values is associative and commutative
hypotheses.rationale: The two summands are syntactically non-identical (different function names and variables) but share the identical algebraic pattern A(z)*B(z)*A(z). A parameterized template captures this common structure with three substitution slots.

hypotheses.construction_plan: Construct a two-dimensional row vector (A(x), B(y)) and a diagonal matrix diag(C(x), D(y)). The matrix product (A(x),B(y)) * diag(C(x),D(y)) * (A(x),B(y))^T expands to A(x)C(x)A(x) + B(y)D(y)B(y). With the substitutions A=V, B=W, C=G0, D=H0, x=p, y=q, this yields the full expression. For the individual summands, set the other vector component to the zero function: the first summand is obtained by B=0, the second by A=0.
required_assumptions: The function values are scalars, so vector and matrix multiplication are standard
The zero function acts as the additive identity for the product
hypotheses.rationale: The sum of two terms of the form A(x)C(x)A(x) and B(y)D(y)B(y) is precisely the quadratic form of a diagonal matrix in the direct sum of the two one-dimensional spaces. This representation change explains the full expression as a single bilinear object and the summands as its diagonal projections.
